title: Sam Darnold’s injury is short term, still no firm timeline, Seahawks say
content:
Seattle Seahawks quarterback Sam Darnold is unlikely to land on injured reserve with a glute injury, though his return timeline remains unclear, leaving his status up in the air for Week 2’s game against the Arizona Cardinals.

A Seahawks spokesperson said Monday that Darnold, who was injured during Wednesday night’s 13-10 win against the New England Patriots, is dealing with a “very unique, soft-tissue injury” that is “short term,” but added there is “no firm timeline.” The Seahawks face the Cardinals in Glendale, Ariz., on Sunday.

The team originally called Darnold’s issue a hip injury, but the spokesperson said Monday that the hip joint was unaffected. On Thursday, coach Mike Macdonald called the injury “more like a muscle thing.”

Avoiding injured reserve would mean Darnold, who departed Wednesday’s game after only five plays, is likely to return within the next four games.

During Monday’s practice, backup Drew Lock and third-stringer Jalen Milroe were the only quarterbacks on the field. The Seahawks’ next practice will be Wednesday.

Speaking Thursday, Macdonald said he didn’t know who would play against the Cardinals in Week 2, but added, “In my mind, I’m kind of thinking Drew is going to play.”

Lock, 29, finished the opener 16 of 22 for 187 yards and a touchdown, plus a 14-yard scramble, as the Seahawks rallied from a 10-0 deficit in the third quarter. His last regular-season start came in 2024 with the New York Giants, where he spent one season between two stints with Seattle.

Also absent from Monday’s practice were linebacker Ernest Jones IV and safety Ty Okada. Jones played all 71 snaps in the season-opening win, while Okada missed the game with a hamstring injury. Rodney Thomas II was elevated from the practice squad and started in his stead.
